value.statement: For a measurable space with measure, real scalar parameter and real-valued F, if the parameter neighborhood s contains x₀, F(τ) is a.e. strongly measurable near x₀, F(x₀) is integrable, F′(x₀) is a.e. strongly measurable, an integrable bound dominates |F′(τ,a)| for almost every a and every τ∈s, F′(τ,a) is the derivative of F(τ,a) for almost every a and every τ∈s, then the integral map has derivative ∫F′(x₀,a), and that derivative function is integrable.

hypotheses: s is a neighborhood of x₀.
F(τ) is a.e. strongly measurable eventually near x₀.
An integrable bound dominates the norm of F′(τ,a) for almost every a and all τ∈s.
For almost every a, τ↦F(τ,a) has derivative F′(τ,a) for every τ∈s.
Real scalar and normed-space structures as in the signature.

value.statement: For continuous u,v on uIcc(a,b), differentiable on the open interval with derivatives u′,v′, and interval-integrable derivatives, the interval integral of u′v+uv′ equals u(b)v(b)−u(a)v(a).

hypotheses: u,v have derivatives u′,v′ on the open interval.
ℝ has the complete normed algebra structure required by the theorem.
